title: Lifting the production cap on coal-fired power stations during the gas crisis (June 2022)
description: On 20 June 2022 Climate and Energy Minister Jetten announced the 'first level' of the gas crisis and said the cabinet would let the three Dutch coal-fired power stations run above the statutory cap of 35% of capacity, a limit set to curb CO2 emissions, to save natural gas before winter as Russia reduced supplies; the measure was to run until 2024 for the time being. According to NOS, his party D66 had until then refused to discuss the coal plants because of the extra CO2 emissions, while coalition partners VVD and CDA had pressed for the change. Jetten said that 'the risk of doing nothing is too great', that the cabinet did not lose sight of its 55% emissions-reduction target for 2030 and that extra climate measures would follow; the cabinet kept €1.9 billion of compensation it would otherwise have paid to plant operators.
key_facts: 20 June 2022: cabinet allows coal plants to run above the 35% cap to save gas
D66 had previously refused to discuss the coal plants (NOS)
Jetten: 'het risico van niets doen is te groot'; additional climate measures promised around Prinsjesdag

title: D66 walks out of talks on the Schoof cabinet's education cuts (December 2024)
description: The Schoof cabinet's 2025 budget contained about €2 billion of cuts to education. Because the PVV–VVD–NSC–BBB coalition lacked a Senate majority, it negotiated with D66, CDA, ChristenUnie, SGP and JA21. On 5 December 2024 D66 leader Jetten pulled out: according to NOS he said the talks had produced good results, such as scrapping the fine for students who take too long to graduate (langstudeerboete), but left too little room for higher teacher salaries and extra money for secondary vocational education (mbo), young scientists and research. The four other parties continued; NOS reported that they were broadly agreed with the coalition on reversing about €700 million of the cuts.
key_facts: 5 December 2024: D66 leaves the education budget talks; CDA, ChristenUnie, SGP and JA21 continue
Jetten cited insufficient room on teacher pay, mbo and research funding
Votes on all budgets postponed by a week

title: Attacks on the D66 party office in The Hague (September 2025 and May 2026)
description: On 20 September 2025, after an anti-immigration demonstration on the Malieveld got out of hand, rioters threw stones through the windows of the D66 party office in The Hague and tried to drive a burning container into it; D66 put the damage at €34,000. On the television programme Buitenhof the next day Jetten called the riots political violence and said the rioters used words also heard in parliament, including from PVV leader Wilders ('Politici planten zaadjes'); caretaker Finance Minister Heinen (VVD) said this linked things that had nothing to do with each other, calling the rioters hooligans. According to NOS, thirty rioters had been convicted by May 2026, including for smashing the office windows. On 7 May 2026 a heavy firework bomb was thrown through the office letterbox during a Young Democrats meeting attended by about 30 people; no one was injured, and Jetten called it 'a cowardly act of intimidation'. The Public Prosecution Service suspects a 37-year-old man of causing an explosion with terrorist intent; at a pro forma hearing in August 2026 he confessed and was to be examined at the Pieter Baan Centre. D66 is the targeted party; Jetten is not a party to these proceedings.
key_facts: 20 September 2025: D66 office damaged during riots after an anti-immigration protest (€34,000 damage according to D66)
Jetten called the riots political violence and linked them to rhetoric in parliament; Heinen (VVD) disagreed
Thirty rioters convicted by May 2026 (NOS)
7 May 2026: firework bomb at the office; suspect detained, prosecuted for an explosion with terrorist intent; Jetten is not a party

title: Remark about Crown Princess Amalia in an election debate (October 2025)
description: At the EenVandaag election debate before about 2,000 students on 27 October 2025, Jetten called Crown Princess Amalia's training as a military reservist the best possible advertising for the armed forces, adding: 'Ik gok dat een aantal kerels hier in de zaal hier wel zin in hebben' (to train with her). Moderator Suzanne Bosman immediately asked: 'Wat is dat nu voor seksistische opmerking?'; CDA leader Bontenbal said afterwards he would not have put it that way. Jetten said after the debate that he found her choice 'oprecht superstoer' and hoped young people would follow her example. NOS later described the remark as a slip in an otherwise almost flawless campaign.
key_facts: 27 October 2025, two days before the election
The moderator called the remark sexist; Bontenbal distanced himself from the wording
No formal apology was reported; Jetten reframed it as praise for her choice

title: Victory claim before the official result and PVV insinuations about the count (October–November 2025)
description: With D66 and the PVV both on 26 seats, Jetten claimed victory on 31 October 2025 after the ANP news agency's election service projected that the PVV could no longer overtake D66, saying he did not want to waste time waiting for the official result. PVV leader Wilders called it 'arrogance' not to wait for the Kiesraad, shared unproven posts alleging irregularities in the count in Zaanstad, Maastricht and Leiden, called the agency 'ANP66' and questioned the Kiesraad's independence. Zaanstad called the claims 'pure onzin'; the Kiesraad said irregularities had been found only in Stein and Westerwolde, where about 260 voters received an invalid ballot. On 4 November Wilders accepted the result and congratulated Jetten, and on 7 November the Kiesraad established the official result: D66 1,790,634 votes, PVV 1,760,966, a margin of 29,668.
key_facts: 31 October 2025: Jetten claims a 'historic' win on the basis of the ANP projection
Wilders' insinuations about the count were rejected by the municipalities concerned and the Kiesraad
7 November 2025: official result confirms D66 as largest party by votes

title: Resignation of D66 informateur Hans Wijers over a leaked private message (November 2025)
description: After the verkenner Wouter Koolmees (D66) advised that D66 and CDA work together first, the two parties named Hans Wijers (D66, a former Economic Affairs minister) and Sybrand Buma (CDA) as informateurs. On 14 November 2025 Wijers stepped down with immediate effect after NRC confronted him with a private message, sent well before the election, in which according to NRC he called VVD leader Dilan Yeşilgöz 'die feeks van de VVD'; Wijers said the remarks could damage his position as an impartial informateur. Jetten thanked him and proposed to the Speaker that the formation continue with Buma as sole informateur.
key_facts: 14 November 2025: Wijers resigns two days after being named
The VVD later joined the D66–CDA coalition as third partner

title: Withdrawal of a D66 state-secretary candidate over an inaccurate CV (February 2026)
description: Nathalie van Berkel, D66's candidate for State Secretary for Finance in the cabinet Jetten was forming, withdrew on 17 February 2026 after de Volkskrant found that her CV on LinkedIn listed studies she had never completed. It happened in the last week of formateur Jetten's interviews with candidate ministers; asked about it, Jetten said 'niemand doet iets foutloos' (NOS). D66 put forward Eelco Eerenberg instead, and the cabinet was sworn in as planned on 23 February 2026.
key_facts: 17 February 2026: Van Berkel withdraws after de Volkskrant's findings on her CV
19 February 2026: Eelco Eerenberg named as the new candidate
Swearing-in of the cabinet not delayed

title: D66 senators vote against asylum bills defended by the Jetten cabinet (April 2026)
description: On 21 April 2026 the Senate voted on three asylum bills inherited from the Schoof cabinet and defended by Asylum and Migration Minister Bart van den Brink (CDA), measures the coalition agreement had said would be carried out. D66 senators voted against all three; D66 senator Dittrich said many of the measures were also in the EU migration pact and that the criminalisation of illegal stay lay 'like a stone on the stomach'. After the amending bill softening that criminalisation was rejected 37–38, CDA also voted against and the Asylum Emergency Measures Act was rejected 31–44, while the two-status system act passed 41–34. 50PLUS senator Van Rooijen spoke of tension between the prime minister and the D66 Senate group and called it 'deeply sad that Jetten is being let down by his own party'.
key_facts: 21 April 2026: Asylum Emergency Measures Act rejected; two-status act adopted
D66 voted against all three bills in the Senate; in 2025 D66 had also voted against the two-status act in the House
Opposition senators pointed to a split between Jetten and his party's senators

title: Planned pension and benefit cuts, union strikes and the cabinet's climb-down (2026)
description: The coalition agreement included about €6.5 billion of long-term savings on social security: a faster rise in the AOW pension age, WW unemployment benefit cut from two years to one and a lower daily wage for WIA disability benefits. In the debate on the agreement GL-PvdA leader Klaver called the AOW plan 'a false start' that broke the 2019 pension agreement with unions and employers. The unions walked out of the first meeting with the cabinet and refused talks while the savings remained in the budget, with actions at Schiphol on 22 June 2026, regional actions and a nationwide public-transport stoppage on 24 June; the employers' federation VNO-NCW also opposed a fixed savings target. The cabinet dropped the faster AOW rise before the summer, scrapped the daily-wage cut and postponed other measures in the September budget, and on 2 October Jetten announced that all the WW, TAO and WIA savings were off the table; according to Jetten the unions then suspended their actions, and a first meeting with unions and employers on a social agreement was set for 7 October at the Catshuis. Asked whether the unions had won, Jetten said no: the need for far-reaching reforms remained.
key_facts: 4 February 2026: motions against the AOW, WW and healthcare-deductible plans rejected; Klaver: 'a false start'
22 May 2026: Jetten still aimed at €6.5 billion of savings but offered to negotiate
22–24 June 2026: union actions including a nationwide public-transport stoppage
2 October 2026: remaining WW, TAO and WIA savings withdrawn; social partners invited to the Catshuis

title: Unrest over new asylum reception centres and criticism of the prime minister's response (2026)
description: Under the Jetten cabinet the shortage of asylum reception places persisted and plans for new or temporary reception centres (azc's) met local resistance; according to the Parliamentary Documentation Centre, protests in Loosdrecht, IJsselstein, Den Bosch and Apeldoorn got out of hand, and the cabinet consulted municipalities and announced a 'flying team' to help them. In late July 2026 homes and cars in Engelen (Den Bosch) were daubed with slogans against a planned reception centre. PRO leader Jesse Klaver accused Jetten of a lack of moral leadership and called his silence 'incomprehensible'; hours later Jetten condemned the 'ugly vandalism', writing that there was 'no justification whatsoever' for intimidating people who help refugees.
key_facts: Protests against reception centres in several municipalities got out of hand (Parlement.com)
29 July 2026: Jetten condemns the vandalism in Engelen after Klaver's call to speak out

title: 'Vol op hun bek slaan' remark at the D66 congress (September 2026)
description: At the D66 congress on 27 September 2026, answering a question from the floor about well-organised groups that deliberately attack the rights of LGBTI people, women and minorities, Jetten said: 'We gaan die lui niet laten winnen, maar we gaan ze vol op hun bek slaan' ('we're going to punch them right in the mouth'). The remark drew criticism, including from parties in the House; commentators called it unworthy of a prime minister, and PVV leader Wilders asked on X whether he could then make comparable statements about immigrants (VRT). The next day Jetten said he should have used more appropriate language, did not mean it literally, called it 'a slip of the tongue' and 'absolutely not a call to use violence' but a call to stand up for Dutch norms and values, and promised to choose his words more carefully.
key_facts: 27 September 2026: remark made in a spontaneous answer at the party congress
28 September 2026: Jetten expresses regret; 'slip of the tongue'

title: First budget without a majority: box 3 financing reversal and PVV no-confidence motion (September–October 2026)
description: The minority cabinet presented its first budget and Tax Plan on 15 September 2026 without an assured majority in either chamber. On the eve of the House debate on the budget (30 September – 1 October), after days of internal coalition talks, it sent a plan to pay for an accelerated capital-gains tax in box 3 partly by taxing more small savers and investors (Jetten said it concerned savings of €50,000 or more, €100,000 for couples). After criticism from opposition and coalition parties, Finance Minister Heinen conceded within a day and a half that he had not thought the financing through and the plan was dropped; Jetten said he could 'imagine that people can no longer keep up', and Deputy PM Yeşilgöz called it 'not a nice week'. In the Senate debate of 6 October a PVV motion of no confidence was rejected, along with all other motions; opposition parties urged the coalition to choose between a left- and a right-wing route to majorities, which Jetten and the coalition leaders declined to do. As of mid-October 2026 the cabinet was still negotiating new financing for box 3 and support for the Tax Plan, on which the House is to vote on 12 November.
key_facts: 15 September 2026: first budget of the Jetten cabinet presented
1 October 2026: plan to tax smaller savers and investors withdrawn
6 October 2026: PVV motion of no confidence rejected in the Senate
House vote on the Tax Plan 2027 scheduled for 12 November 2026
